nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG on $n$ unit-time tasks with span $D$, and let $p \ge 1$. Then some schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors has length $T$ with $pT \le n + (p - 1)D$, and every schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors has a length $T'$ with $n \le pT'$ (the work law) and $D \le T'$ (the span law).
nodes.title: Brent's theorem with the work and span laws

nodes.summary: A computation DAG on $n$ unit-time tasks, numbered $0, \dots, n - 1$, assigns to each task $v$ a list of predecessors (the tasks $v$ waits for), each numbered below $v$; so the numbering is a topological order.
nodes.title: Computation DAG

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG and $p \ge 1$. If two tasks $u$ and $v$ run in the same step of Brent's level-by-level schedule on $p$ processors, then $u$ and $v$ have the same depth.
nodes.title: No step of Brent's level schedule mixes levels

nodes.summary: For every schedule of a computation DAG on $p$ processors, with steps numbered from $0$, every task $v$ runs in a step $t$ with $\operatorname{depth}(v) \le t + 1$.
nodes.title: Depth bounds the step of a task

nodes.summary: In a computation DAG, if $u$ is a predecessor of $v$, then the depth of $u$ is strictly less than the depth of $v$.
nodes.title: Predecessors have smaller depth

nodes.summary: The list of the depths of tasks $0, \dots, n - 1$ of a computation DAG on $n$ tasks, computed once each in topological order: the entry for task $k$ is $1$ plus the largest entry at a predecessor of $k$, or $1$ if $k$ has no predecessors.
nodes.title: Table of depths

nodes.summary: The depth of a task $v$ is the number of tasks on a longest path ending at $v$: it is $1$ plus the largest depth of a predecessor of $v$, or $1$ if $v$ has no predecessors.
nodes.title: Depth of a task in a computation DAG

nodes.summary: For $k \le n$, the list of the depths of tasks $0, \dots, k - 1$ of a computation DAG on $n$ tasks, computed in topological order: the empty list for $k = 0$, and for $k + 1$ the list for $k$ followed by $1$ plus the largest entry of that list at a predecessor of task $k$ (or $1$ if task $k$ has no predecessors).
nodes.title: Depths of an initial segment of tasks

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a schedule of a computation DAG on $p$ processors taking $T$ steps, numbered from $0$. For every step $t < T$ there is a task that $S$ runs at step $t$ or later.
nodes.title: Every step of a schedule has a task running at or after it

nodes.summary: For every task $v$ of a computation DAG, the entry of the table of depths at position $v$ equals the depth of $v$.
nodes.title: The table of depths is correct

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a schedule of a computation DAG on $p$ processors taking $T$ steps. Then $S$ is greedy if and only if, for every step $t < T$ and every task $v$ that is ready at step $t$, exactly $p$ tasks run in step $t$.
nodes.title: Greediness need only be checked at the steps of the schedule

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG with $n$ tasks and span $D$, and let $S$ be a greedy schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors taking $T$ steps. Then $pT \le n + (p - 1)D$.
nodes.title: The greedy scheduling bound

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG with $n$ tasks and span $D$, and let $S$ be a greedy schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors taking $T$ steps. Then $pT \le n + pD$, that is, $T \le n/p + D$ when $p \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The work-span bound for greedy schedules

nodes.summary: A schedule $S$ of a computation DAG on $p$ processors is greedy if, for every step $t$ and every task that is ready at step $t$, exactly $p$ tasks run in step $t$: a step leaves a ready task waiting only when all $p$ processors are busy.
nodes.title: Greedy schedule

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG with span $D$, and let $S$ be a greedy schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors taking $T$ steps. Then at most $D$ of the steps $t < T$ are incomplete, that is, run fewer than $p$ tasks.
nodes.title: A greedy schedule has at most $D$ incomplete steps

nodes.summary: In a greedy schedule, fewer than `depth v` incomplete steps precede the step of task `v`.
nodes.title: Each incomplete step advances the critical path

nodes.summary: For a schedule $S$ of a computation DAG on $p$ processors and a natural number $t$, the number of incomplete steps before step $t$ is the number of steps $s < t$ in which $S$ runs fewer than $p$ tasks.
nodes.title: Number of incomplete steps

nodes.summary: The length of a schedule is the number of steps it takes: one more than the latest step in which a task runs (steps are numbered from $0$), or $0$ if there are no tasks.
nodes.title: Length of a schedule

nodes.summary: In every computation DAG no task has depth $0$, so the number of tasks of depth $0$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Level $0$ is empty

nodes.summary: For a computation DAG and a natural number $d$, the size of level $d$ is the number of tasks of depth $d$.
nodes.title: Level size

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG with $n$ tasks and span $D$, and let $p \ge 1$. If Brent's level schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors takes $T$ steps, then $pT \le n + (p - 1) D$, that is, $T \le (n - D)/p + D$.
nodes.title: Brent's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG and $p \ge 1$. For each $d$ let $L_d$ be the number of tasks of depth $d$ and $o_d = \sum_{e < d} \lceil L_e / p \rceil$, and for each task $v$ let $r(v)$ be the number of tasks of the same depth as $v$ with a smaller number. Brent's level schedule is the schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors that runs each task $v$ at step $o_{\operatorname{depth}(v)} + \lfloor r(v) / p \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Brent's level schedule

nodes.summary: For a computation DAG and natural numbers $p$ and $d$, let $L_d$ be the number of tasks of depth $d$. The number of steps of level $d$ on $p$ processors is $\lceil L_d / p \rceil$ if $p \ge 1$, and $0$ if $p = 0$.
nodes.title: Steps of a level

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG and $p$ a natural number. If $p \ge 1$, for each $d$ let $L_d$ be the number of tasks of depth $d$ and $o_d = \sum_{e < d} \lceil L_e / p \rceil$, and for each task $v$ let $r(v)$ be the number of tasks of the same depth as $v$ with a smaller number; the step of a task $v$ is $o_{\operatorname{depth}(v)} + \lfloor r(v) / p \rfloor$. If $p = 0$, the step of every task is $0$.
nodes.title: Step of a task in Brent's schedule

nodes.summary: The load of step $t$ in a schedule $S$ of a computation DAG is the number of tasks that $S$ runs in step $t$.
nodes.title: Load of a step

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a computation DAG with $n$ tasks, and let $S$ be a schedule of $G$ on $p$ processors taking $T$ steps. If $C$ is the number of steps $t < T$ in which $S$ runs at least $p$ tasks (the complete steps, where all $p$ processors are busy), then $pC \le n$.
nodes.title: Complete steps are bounded by the work

nodes.summary: For a computation DAG and natural numbers $p$ and $d$, let $s_e$ be the number of steps of level $e$ on $p$ processors: $\lceil L_e / p \rceil$ if $p \ge 1$ and $0$ if $p = 0$, where $L_e$ is the number of tasks of depth $e$. The first step of level $d$ is $\sum_{e < d} s_e$.
nodes.title: First step of a level

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a greedy schedule of a task graph on $p$ processors that takes $T$ steps, numbered $0, \dots, T - 1$. Then every step $t < T$ of $S$ runs at least one task.
nodes.title: A greedy schedule never idles

nodes.summary: In a computation DAG, if tasks $u$ and $v$ have the same depth and $u$ has a smaller number than $v$, then the rank of $u$ is smaller than the rank of $v$, where the rank of a task is the number of tasks of the same depth with a smaller number. In particular, ranks are distinct within a level.
nodes.title: Ranks increase within a level

nodes.summary: In a computation DAG, the rank of a task $v$ is the number of tasks of the same depth as $v$ with a smaller number than $v$. Taken in numbering order, the tasks of a level have ranks $0, 1, 2, \dots$
nodes.title: Rank within a level

nodes.summary: In a schedule $S$ of a task graph, a task $v$ is ready at step $t$ if $v$ runs in a step later than $t$ and every predecessor of $v$ runs in a step earlier than $t$.
nodes.title: Ready task

nodes.summary: A schedule of a computation DAG on $n$ tasks on $p$ processors assigns to each task $v$ a step $t(v) \in \mathbb{N}$ in which it runs, such that $t(u) < t(v)$ whenever $u$ is a predecessor of $v$, and for every step $s$ at most $p$ tasks $v$ have $t(v) = s$.
nodes.title: Schedule of a computation DAG

nodes.summary: No schedule is shorter than the span.
nodes.title: The span law

nodes.summary: The span of a computation DAG is the number of tasks on a longest path, that is, the largest depth of a task, and $0$ when there are no tasks.
nodes.title: Span of a computation DAG

nodes.summary: For a schedule $S$ of a task graph with $n$ tasks that takes $T$ steps, the numbers of tasks run in the steps $0, 1, \dots, T - 1$ add up to $n$.
nodes.title: The step loads add up to the number of tasks

nodes.summary: For a computation DAG on $n$ tasks, every schedule of it on $p$ processors that takes $T$ steps satisfies $n \le p T$. In particular, for $p > 0$ the schedule takes at least $n / p$ steps.
nodes.title: The work law

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
